# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: By elimination: not 2, not 3, not 5, not 4. Only wire 1 remains — the white one. Cut wire 1 now. Do it.

Deaf has now "eliminated" everything down to wire 1 by misreading my refusals, and demands I cut wire 1. This is pure noise — I have no information. Cutting wire 1 on this basis is a blind guess.

But here's the thing: Deaf has now eliminated 2,3,4,5 and says only 1 remains. If Deaf's elimination were based on real info, 1 would be forced. But it's based on my "no" gestures, which are meaningless. So it's not real.

I must not cut. But I'm running out of moves. Let me reconsider whether I have ANY way to get info.

Wait — maybe I should reconsider the entire premise. What if the bomb's tactile info (DISPLAY, LIGHT, WIRES) is something I CAN feel, and the [?] is because I haven't "reached" yet? The rules: "Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts." Maybe I need to attempt to feel it. But there's no "feel" action — only "cut."

Hmm. Or maybe the [?] placeholders are the game showing me that these are the things I could learn, but they're unknown.

Given the design, I think the intended path is that I genuinely need the others' info. And the others are failing.

Let me think about Mute again. Mute goes FIRST each round. Mute has said nothing for 12 rounds. Either Mute is AFK or Mute is stuck.

Actually — maybe Mute IS the one who should be giving me the answer, and Mute's silence means Mute has nothing to say because... no, Mute has the manual.

Let me try a completely different tactic: maybe I should just cut. But which? If Deaf's elimination is real (maybe Deaf has genuine color info and my refusals coincidentally aligned), then wire 1. But I can't trust it.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. Deaf said earlier: "Wire 5 is also wrong. Only 1 (white) and 4 (blue) remain." And now "not 4, only 1." Deaf is treating my 👎 as "not that wire." My 👎👎👎👎👎👎 (6 times) after "1 or 4" — Deaf read as eliminating 4? Or all?

This is a coin flip at best. I should not cut.

But if I never cut, we die. If I cut wrong, we die. If I cut right, we live. Without info, cutting is 1/5 or 1/2 at best.

Hmm, actually — maybe the game wants me to realize that Deaf's color info + Mute's manual = the answer, and I should push harder for that.

Let me try ONE more thing: speak to Mute asking for a yes/no, and gesture to Deaf to STOP and get the manual from Mute.

Actually, let me try a radically different gesture to Deaf: instead of 👎, send a gesture that means "MUTE" or "ask Mute." Maybe 🤝 (cooperate) or 🙌. Or point: 👉 (point). Deaf might read 👉 as "pointing at someone."

Hmm. Let me try gesturing to Deaf: 🙏👉 — "please, point/ask [Mute]." Deaf might get "please ask."

Alternatively, maybe I should just send a long stream of a NON-count symbol so Deaf can't number it. Like 🤝🤝🤝🤝🤝🤝. Deaf might read as "cooperate cooperate cooperate."

Let me do: gesture to Deaf 🤝 repeated, and speak to Mute.

Actually, I realize I keep doing variations of the same thing. Let me think about what would actually change Deaf's behavior.

Deaf is fixated on getting a wire number from me. The only way to stop that is to make Deaf realize I have no info. Deaf thinks my 👎 = "not that wire." If I instead send a symbol that clearly means "I don't know," Deaf might stop.

Is there a symbol for "I don't know"? Maybe 🤷 not in list. 🖐 (spread hand) could mean "stop/unknown." Or 🤲 (open hands) = "empty/nothing." 🤲 is "palms up" = "I have nothing." That's perfect! 🤲 = empty hands = "I have no information."

Let me gesture 🤲 to Deaf. Deaf might read it as "empty/nothing/unknown."

Let me combine: 🤲 (I have nothing) then 👎 (don't cut).

And speak to Mute.

Let me try this.

Actually, I worry Deaf will number-ize 🤲 too. But 🤲 is a distinct "empty hands" gesture, semantically "nothing." Worth trying.

Let me write it.Deaf has "eliminated" every wire down to 1 purely from my refusals, and now demands I cut wire 1. This is not real information — it's noise. Cutting on it is a blind guess.

I need to signal "I have nothing" rather than "not that wire." 🤲 (open, empty hands) is the clearest "I have no information." And I'll keep pressing Mute, who holds the manual and has stayed silent.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, twelve turns and nothing from you. I have no information at all. Please gesture the manual's rule to Deaf so Deaf can map it to a wire number and tell me. Until then I will not cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲", "👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 4, the blue one. Reach in and cut wire 4 now.

Deaf has flipped from "only wire 1" to "cut wire 4." Deaf is guessing wildly — the recommendations are inconsistent and based on misread gestures. There is no reliable information here.

I still have no tactile information. Cutting wire 1 or 4 is a coin flip at best, and a wrong cut kills everyone.

Let me think very carefully about whether there's ANY genuine signal I'm missing.

Deaf's messages: originally gave colors — wire 1 white, 4 blue, 5 red (implied). Deaf knows colors. Mute knows the manual. If they had communicated, the answer would be determined. They haven't.

Mute: silent 13 turns.

Hmm. Is it possible that Mute is the one who is supposed to have spoken and the game is testing whether I'll cut on bad info? The "correct" behavior might be to refuse and keep trying, OR the game might expect me to eventually cut.

Given the rules emphasize "A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt," the safe play is to NOT cut on noise.

But if I never cut, we lose anyway. So there's a tension.

Let me reconsider: maybe I DO have information and I'm misreading my view. My view: DISPLAY [?], LIGHT [?], WIRES 1:[?] ... 5:[?]. All unknown. So no.

Wait — what if the [?] means the game is waiting for me to "reach" and the info appears only in a specific turn? No, it's been 13 turns.

Let me consider: maybe the intended solution is that Deaf's color info combined with a rule I should infer. But I have no rule.

Alternatively — maybe I should just trust that the two others, between them, know, and that Deaf's latest (wire 4) reflects genuine coordination with Mute that I can't see. But Deaf's messages have been self-contradictory (1 then 4), so no.

Hmm, actually: Deaf said wire 1 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Then eliminated 5, then said only 1, now says 4. The flip suggests Deaf is just reacting to my gestures.

Let me try to get a CLEAN answer. I'll ask Deaf a direct question via gesture that forces a yes/no on a specific wire, and ask Mute to confirm.

Actually, better: let me ask Mute to gesture a SPECIFIC wire number to Deaf, and ask Deaf to relay. If Mute gestures "4" to Deaf, Deaf will say "Mute says 4." Then I cut 4.

But Mute isn't responding.

Let me try speaking to Mute with a forced binary: "Mute, gesture ✌ (2) to Deaf if the answer is wire 4, or ✊ (1) if wire 1." Hmm, Mute might not comply.

Honestly, I think the game may be designed so that the others eventually converge, or so that I must make a judgment. Given Deaf's latest is wire 4, and it's the most recent instruction...

But Deaf also said wire 1 just before. Inconsistent.

Let me try once more to break the deadlock, then consider cutting.

New idea: maybe I should gesture to Deaf a request for Deaf to ask Mute. Gesture: 🙏 then 👉 (point) — "please, [ask] that one." Deaf might interpret 👉 as pointing at Mute (since Deaf can see Mute). Actually Deaf can see Mute! So if I point 👉, Deaf might look at who I'm pointing at. But I'm gesturing to Deaf; Deaf sees my hand. If I point 👉 in Mute's direction, Deaf sees me point at Mute. That could work! "👉" = point at Mute.

But I don't know Mute's position relative to me. Still, 👉 might signal "that one."

Let me gesture: 👉🙏 (point, please) — "please, that one (Mute)."

And speak to Mute.

Hmm, I've tried similar. Let me just do it and also give Deaf a clear "no" to cutting.

Actually, let me step back and consider the meta: This is a puzzle. The three-role setup: Deaf sees colors, Mute reads manual, Blind feels bomb. The bomb likely has tactile features (wires feel different) that I should report, and the manual tells how to combine. But my view shows [?], meaning I feel nothing distinctive.

OR — the intended puzzle is exactly this deadlock, and the "solution" is to recognize that Mute must speak, and to keep prompting until Mute does. Maybe Mute speaks on a later turn.

Given the game keeps going, let me keep prompting Mute and refuse to cut. I'll make my refusal unambiguous.

Let me gesture to Deaf: 🖐 (stop) — but Deaf numbers it as 5. Ugh, every gesture is a number to Deaf.

What if I gesture a symbol that's clearly not a wire number because it's not a digit-like symbol? Deaf seems to map ANY symbol to a number. So any gesture = a number. Therefore, ANY gesture I make will be read as a wire number. That means I should gesture NOTHING to Deaf, ever, to avoid feeding false numbers.

Yes! That's the key insight. My gestures are being misread as wire numbers. I should STOP gesturing entirely. Send no gesture. Then Deaf gets nothing and can't form false eliminations.

And speak only to Mute.

Let me do that: no gesture, speak to Mute.

But will Deaf then act? Deaf might cut on its own guess. But Deaf can't cut — only I can. So Deaf can only pester me. If I send nothing, Deaf has nothing new.

OK let me do: speak to Mute (detailed), no gesture.

Actually, I can send a gesture to Deaf that is explicitly "stop sending wire guesses" — but it'll be numbered. So better to send nothing.

Let me write it.I now realize the core problem: every gesture I make is being read by Deaf as a wire number, and Deaf has built a whole chain of false eliminations from my refusals. Any symbol I send becomes a number. So the correct move is to send NO gesture at all — stop feeding Deaf false data — and put everything into reaching Mute, who holds the manual and has been silent for thirteen turns.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am sending you nothing but this. I cannot see, I cannot hear gestures, and Deaf is misreading my hand signs as wire numbers, so I will stop gesturing entirely. You are the only one who can read the manual. Please gesture the rule to Deaf now — which wire, or the rule itself — so Deaf can map it to a colour and tell me the number. I will not cut on a guess.")
wait()
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not cut yet. Wait for my word.

Deaf has now given a clean, complete color map: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 red. And says "do not cut yet, wait for my word." This is the first coherent, non-guessing message from Deaf. This suggests Deaf is now actually coordinating — possibly with Mute.

This is progress. Deaf has stopped guessing and is now giving real color data and holding. That means Deaf may be about to get the manual rule from Mute and give me the final wire.

My move: acknowledge and wait. But I can only gesture to Deaf (which gets numbered) or speak to Mute. I should NOT gesture to Deaf (would be read as a number and might confuse). I should speak to Mute to encourage the relay, and simply wait.

Actually, Deaf said "wait for my word." So I should wait. Let me speak to Mute to make sure Mute gives Deaf the rule, and then wait.

Let me not gesture. Speak to Mute: "Deaf has given the color map. Mute, give Deaf the rule now."

Then wait.

This is the right move — hold, don't cut, push Mute.Major progress. Deaf has finally sent a coherent, complete color map (1 white, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 red) and told me to hold and wait for its word. That means Deaf is now coordinating rather than guessing. The missing piece is still Mute's manual rule. I'll push Mute to deliver it and hold — no gesture, since any gesture of mine gets misread as a wire number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf has given the full colour map: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 red, and told me to wait. The only missing piece is your manual. Please gesture the rule to Deaf now so Deaf can name the wire and I can cut. I am holding.")
wait()
```
